sections.overview: This conspicuous American damselfly ranges from southern Canada through the United States to Honduras, making it the most widespread North American species in its genus.
sections.identification: Males have a bright red patch at the base of each wing, while the rest of the body is metallic green; females are less vividly marked.
sections.habitat: Adults perch beside gently flowing, sunny streams and rivers, often on vegetation overhanging the banks.
sections.diet: Adults catch small flying insects from a perch, and the aquatic larvae prey on smaller invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Males defend streamside territories that provide perches and access to females; territoriality has been studied directly in this species.
sections.reproduction: After mating, females insert eggs into submerged vegetation in flowing water, where the young develop as aquatic larvae.
sections.ecology: The smoky rubyspot Hetaerina titia is a congener with darker wings. Genetic work also finds deep lineage structure within H. americana.
sections.conservation: Genetic differentiation between watersheds suggests conservation planning should consider variation across its broad range.
